newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Parole Commission to restrict computer access.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Parole Commission to restrict computer access.

text.p: The U.S. Parole Commission will restrict computer use by certain high-risk, convicted criminals who have been released from prison on parole, the Justice Department said Monday.

It said the panel made the decision Dec. 4 after noting that information was available on the Internet and computer online services involving such offenses as child molestation, hate crimes and illegal use of explosives.

"Unrestricted access to the Internet and other computer online services can provide sophisticated offenders with new opportunities for crime and criminal associations," Edward Reilly, the commission chairman, said.
"We cannot ignore the possibility that such offenders may be tempted to use computer services to repeat their crimes," he said in a statement.
Those on parole already face numerous limits on travel, association and other activites. The commission now has the discretionary power to restrict computer use.

For example, a person on parole may be required to get written approval from the commission to use an Internet provider, bulletin board system or any other computer network, the Justice Department said.
It said other conditions could include requiring unannounced examinations of the computer by a probation officer, keeping a daily log of computer use and installing equipment that monitors use.
The restrictions would be decided on a case-by-case basis.
